column3: “Jesus” supplies the unnamed subject, and “began” is supplied; the Greek coordinates picking and eating while rubbing.
The Greek strengthens the question with “not even this.”
The Greek names eating before giving to his companions; BSB reverses those actions. “Consecrated bread” renders the Greek “bread of presentation.”
“Jesus” supplies the subject; “among us” renders the Greek “into the midst.”
“The man” makes the Greek pronoun explicit.
“The scribes and Pharisees” makes the Greek pronoun explicit; “began” is supplied.
“Son” before Alphaeus makes the relationship explicit where the critical text has only a genitive.
“Son” before James makes the relationship explicit where the Greek has only a genitive.
“Jesus” and “was there” supply the subject and a predicate for the crowd clause.
The Greek first says “Blessed the poor” and then addresses them as “yours”; BSB makes the first clause directly “you.”
The critical text lacks a separate “to you” after “woe,” though it directly mentions people speaking of “you.”
The Greek describes those currently hearing, rather than future “will listen.”
